## Slide 1: Overview of the Analysis

**Objective** - Analyze food consumption data from Peru's National Household Survey (ENAHO) - Evaluate the impact of nutritional intervention programs (CRECER, JUNTOS)

**Data Source** - Annual data: 2007–2016 (10-year period) - Survey subjects: Household food group consumption quantities - Complex sample survey design reflected in analysis

**Major Processing Stages** 1. Data preparation and processing 2. Verification and quality management 3. Basic statistical analysis

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Slide 2: Part 1 – Data Preparation (file1.txt)

**Step 1: Calculate Household Composition (Function `get_familysize_ame`)** - Age calculation: Computed from birth month/year to current month/year - Adult Male Equivalent (AME): Apply coefficients by sex and age group - Output: Household family size and AME-standardized values

**Step 2: Aggregate Food Group Consumption (Function `get_food_consumption_family`)** - Load consumption units and frequency from survey records - Apply gram conversion coefficients - Aggregate into 8 food groups based on food classification

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Slide 3: Part 1 – Data Preparation (continued)

**Step 3: Convert to Per Capita Consumption (Function `get_food_consumption_capita`)** - Divide household-level consumption by AME - Calculate per capita per day food group consumption

**Step 4: Attach Geographic and Income Information** - Geographic classification: Coast (Costa) / Highland (Sierra) / Amazon (Selva) - Department codes, urban/rural classification - Intervention status: Classified by program start year (2009, 2011)

**Step 5: Log Transformation and Score Calculation** - log1p transformation: Handle zero values - Recommended intake score: Adequate (1) / Excess (2) / Insufficient (3)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Slide 4: Part 1 – Overall Processing Flow

```         
Annual Loop (2007-2016)
│
├─ Load mod1 (basic info), mod4 (household composition)
├─ Load mod5 (JUNTOS info), mod7 (food consumption)
│
├─ Calculate family size and AME
│  └─ Apply adult male equivalent coefficients
│
├─ Aggregate food consumption
│  └─ Household-level → Per capita consumption
│
├─ Integrate geographic and economic information
│  ├─ Assign region, department, intervention status
│  └─ Integrate income and JUNTOS participation
│
└─ Final processing
   ├─ Log transformation
   ├─ Score calculation
   └─ Save as annual integrated dataset
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Slide 5: Part 2 – Data Verification (file2.txt)

**Process 1: Set up svydesign** - Reflect complex sample design: PSU (conglomerate), stratum (ESTRATO), weight (FACTOR07) - Calculate income quintiles: Group using weighted quantiles

**Process 2: Outlier Detection (Function `detect_outliers_weighted` × 2 iterations)** - Weighted IQR method for outlier detection - Flexible group-wise outlier identification (region × income or urban/rural × income) - Record detection results: Count and proportion of outliers

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Slide 6: Part 2 – Data Verification (continued)

**Process 3: Recalculate Scores** - Recalculate food scores on dataset after outlier removal - Save two patterns of outlier-treated results: - Pattern 1: Region × Income Quintile - Pattern 2: Urban/Rural Area × Income Quintile

**Process 4: Confirm Basic Statistics** - Use gtsummary/gt packages for descriptive statistics - Compare by group (treatment group/control group, treatment year, etc.) - Calculate mean and standard error for each cell

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Slide 7: Part 2 – Quality Assurance Process

```         
Data Verification Pipeline
│
├─ Create svydesign
│  └─ Reflect complex sample design
│
├─ Outlier Detection and Removal (1st iteration)
│  ├─ Group by region × income quintile
│  ├─ Identify outliers using weighted IQR
│  └─ Recalculate scores
│
├─ Outlier Detection and Removal (2nd iteration)
│  ├─ Group by urban/rural × income quintile
│  ├─ Validate with finer geographic stratification
│  └─ Recalculate scores
│
└─ Confirm Basic Statistics
   ├─ Generate descriptive statistics tables
   ├─ Compare by groups
   └─ Save cleaned dataset
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Slide 8: Key Functions and Processing Content

| Function Name | File | Primary Process |
|--------------------------|----------------|------------------------------|
| `get_familysize_ame()` | file1 | Family size using adult male equivalent |
| `get_food_consumption_family()` | file1 | Aggregate food group consumption |
| `get_food_consumption_capita()` | file1 | Convert to per capita consumption |
| `add_food_score()` | file1/2 | Calculate recommendation-based scores |
| `detect_outliers_weighted()` | file2 | Weighted outlier detection |
| `set_na_outlier()` | file2 | Replace outliers with NA |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Slide 9: Output Data and Storage Format

**Major Files After Processing**

| File Name | Content | Format |
|----------------------------|-----------------------|---------------------|
| `df_foodgrp_consumption_all_org.rds` | Annual integrated processed data | RDS |
| `df_foodgrp_consumption_clean2.rds` | Final cleaned dataset | RDS |
| `food_consumption_by_area_income.rds` | Basic statistics by area × income | RDS |
| `enaho_files_list.rds` | File path management for each year | RDS |

**Available Variables for Analysis** - Food consumption: Raw data + log1p-transformed version - Scores: 3-level classification + adequacy indicator - Grouping variables: Region, department, income quintile, treatment group

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Slide 10: Next Steps and Considerations

**Preparation for Analysis** - Use cleaned data (`clean2`) - Apply statistical tests reflecting complex sample design (survey package) - Utilize svydesign structure for between-group mean comparisons

**Primary Analysis Methods** - Descriptive statistics: Stratified aggregation using svyby - Causal inference: Difference-in-Differences (pre/post treatment × treatment/control) - Regression analysis: Weighted logistic regression accounting for complex sample design

**Ensure Data Quality** - Verify appropriateness of outlier removal - Confirm sample size by group - Understand missing data patterns
